title: Calendar MCP And Reminder Backbone Roadmap
goal: Turn calendar, todo reminders, scheduled digests and Telegram notifications into one coherent owner-scoped calendar/reminder capability with a built-in MCP server behind it.
why_now: Telegram reminder and todo automation works, but it is still too easy for the AI to create multiple scheduled tasks for one user intent.
Calendar CRUD, CalDAV/Nextcloud sync, CalDAV writeback, note due reminders and scheduled task delivery already exist but are not exposed through one shared capability contract.
A calendar MCP server gives API and local models the same tool surface and makes later Codex/Odysseus verification cleaner.

target_architecture.primary_storage: SQLite calendar, notes and scheduled_tasks tables remain source of truth.
target_architecture.external_sync: CalDAV/Nextcloud remains the calendar backbone for real calendars.
target_architecture.capability_layer: src/calendar_capability_service.py normalizes calendar events, reminders and digests.
target_architecture.mcp_layer: mcp_servers/calendar_server.py exposes read resources and gated write tools.
target_architecture.telegram_role: Telegram is a remote operator channel for reminders, confirmations and status, not the storage backend.
target_architecture.ui_role: No new UI in this track; future UI can call the same capability service and MCP-backed diagnostics.

target_user_stories.request: Schick mir montags bis freitags um 9 Uhr meine Todo-Liste per Telegram.
target_user_stories.expected_result: One scheduled task with a cron or normalized weekday schedule, output_target=telegram, owner timezone resolved, and no duplicate per-day tasks.

target_user_stories.request: Erinnere mich 15 Minuten vor dem Zahnarzttermin.
target_user_stories.expected_result: Calendar event and reminder are linked, CalDAV writeback is attempted when applicable, and Telegram notification delivery is routed through the safe notification boundary.
AI reads a bounded owner-scoped agenda resource, summarizes events and due notes, and does not mutate state.
Telegram can update the existing reminder/task after resolving the target and confirmation, instead of creating a duplicate.

slice_queue.goal: Inventory existing calendar, note reminder, scheduled task, Telegram delivery and CalDAV writeback behavior.
slice_queue.done_when: The roadmap has an accurate current-state section and lists reuse points instead of duplicating storage.
slice_queue.evidence: Current foundation mapped to calendar_routes, caldav_sync/writeback, task_scheduler, task delivery, native tools and built-in MCP server patterns.

slice_queue.goal: Add a pure backend calendar capability service that normalizes list/create/update/delete events, reminders, todo digest schedules and readiness reports.
slice_queue.done_when: The service returns structured owner-scoped results and can represent agenda, reminders, digest schedules and writeback readiness without Telegram-specific assumptions.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/calendar_capability_service.py with agenda, readiness and todo-digest schedule-plan contracts; tests/test_calendar_capability_service.py covers owner scope, single weekday cron plan and redacted readiness.

slice_queue.goal: Ensure weekday and recurring reminders collapse into one scheduled task when possible instead of creating one task per weekday.
slice_queue.done_when: Mo-Fr 09:00 todo digest is represented as one cron/schedule task, target updates edit the existing task, and duplicate prevention is covered by tests.
slice_queue.evidence: manage_tasks create now normalizes weekly/weekday creates into one canonical cron task and merges repeated compatible weekday creates into the existing task; focused tests cover cron normalization, five weekly creates collapsing to one task, and duplicate todo_digest reuse.

slice_queue.goal: Add a built-in calendar MCP server with read-only agenda, reminders and readiness resources first.
slice_queue.done_when: MCP tools/resources can list today's agenda, upcoming events, reminders and readiness without exposing private raw content or cross-owner data.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented mcp_servers/calendar_server.py with read-only agenda, reminders and readiness tools/resources, fail-closed owner scoping, and Built-in: Calendar registration; tests/test_mcp_calendar_server.py covers tools, resources, owner scope and registration.

slice_queue.goal: Expose MCP write tools for calendar events, reminders and digest schedules with confirmation gates for create/update/delete where appropriate.
slice_queue.done_when: Writes require owner scope and confirmation for destructive changes, return structured content, and never persist chat ids, tokens or raw private prompts.
slice_queue.evidence: Calendar MCP now exposes confirmation-gated event, reminder and todo-digest write tools, requires an owner for writes, routes through existing manage_calendar/manage_notes/manage_tasks logic, and tests cover confirmation blocking, owner-scoped event/reminder writes, delete gating and single cron digest creation without token/chat-id leakage.

slice_queue.goal: Route Telegram reminder and todo automation through the capability service so mobile commands inspect/update existing reminders before creating new ones.
slice_queue.done_when: Telegram can ask status, create a reminder, update a reminder and receive precise feedback when clarification or confirmation is needed.
slice_queue.evidence: Telegram control commands now cover /calendar, /agenda, /reminders, /remind create/update and /todo digest; they use calendar capability service helpers, avoid agent turns for control commands, create one canonical Telegram todo-digest task for Mo-Fr schedules, and focused tests cover status, create, update and duplicate-safe digest behavior.

slice_queue.goal: Expose CalDAV/Nextcloud sync and writeback health as calendar readiness diagnostics.
slice_queue.done_when: Readiness reports configured accounts, sync windows, pending writebacks and last errors in redacted form.

slice_queue.goal: Run one bounded live smoke on Debian: create or update a harmless Telegram todo digest/reminder and verify delivery/status.
slice_queue.done_when: A harmless reminder/digest is scheduled, visible through MCP readiness/status, and Telegram receives the expected message without duplicate tasks.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve a harmless live Telegram reminder/digest smoke on Debian with exact wording and delivery target.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: A test reminder could notify the wrong channel or duplicate real user tasks.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve a harmless calendar create/update/delete against the intended Nextcloud/CalDAV test calendar.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: Calendar writes could modify a real calendar unexpectedly.

success_metrics: Mo-Fr todo digest is one task, not five.
Agenda reads combine calendar events, due notes and scheduled reminders in one owner-scoped response.
Calendar MCP has read-only resources and gated write tools.
Telegram can remotely inspect and control reminders without becoming the primary backend.
Nextcloud/CalDAV readiness is visible and redacted.
No tokens, chat ids, host paths or raw private content are persisted.
